substory_punchline: Within-ecotype, within-substudy meta-analysis surfaces six actionable pathobionts that replicate at 88% on a held-out cohort

content.punchline: Within-ecotype, within-substudy meta-analysis surfaces six actionable pathobionts that replicate at 88% on a held-out cohort

slides.speaker_notes_seed: Lead in from S1's close: 'the ecotypes are a usable framework, not bit-reproducible — the operational question is whether the targets inside each ecotype replicate.' Answer that directly here: the answer is yes, at 88.2%, on a genuinely held-out cohort. The key methodological move is the within-ecotype × within-substudy design — it strips the confound that naive cross-cohort DA would carry. This section covers how the analysis was designed (position 1), what it found (positions 2–3), and where the honest limits are (position 4).

content.title: Within-ecotype × within-substudy design strips cross-cohort confounds from target discovery

step_caption: Ecotype stratification isolates biologically comparable subpopulations before DA
Within-substudy contrast removes cohort-specific technical and dietary confounds
Four-criteria NB05 scoring (literature + engraftment + strain-adaptation + BGC) thresholds to 6 actionable targets

slides.speaker_notes_seed: The critical design choice is nesting: DA is run within ecotype AND within substudy simultaneously. Naive cross-cohort DA conflates population-composition differences between studies (geography, diet, medication) with disease signal. NB04e uses 4 IBD sub-studies that each have both CD and nonIBD arms; E1 DA runs on HallAB_2017 + NielsenHB_2014 (82 CD / 280 nonIBD), yielding 51 sign-concordant candidates. NB05 then applies 4 criteria: literature/cohort CD-association (A3), protective-analog exclusion (A4), engraftment evidence (A5), BGC inflammatory mediator (A6). The 2.5 threshold selects 6 of 71 scored candidates. REPORT §5g + §5h.

content.subtitle: E1 Tier-A candidates sign-concordant on independently held-out HMP2 cohort
content.sub_pointer: 45 of 51 E1 candidates are CD↑ in both discovery and held-out HMP2 (n=130 subjects)
content.source_footer: REPORT.md §5f (NB04h); HMP2 not in CMD_IBD training set

slides.speaker_notes_seed: This is the deck's strongest credibility number. HMP2 (HMP_2019_ibdmdb) was explicitly held out — it was absent from the CMD_IBD sub-study list used for training. The comparison uses the same MetaPhlAn3 namespace, so there is no Kaiju↔MetaPhlAn3 fragility (unlike the UC Davis GMM projection). Within HMP2-projected E1 samples (593 CD / 337 nonIBD), 45/51 E1 Tier-A candidates are sign-concordant. Only two top-20 candidates fail: S. thermophilus (possibly dairy exposure artifact in HMP2) and Bacteroides stercoris (n.s.). REPORT §5f verbatim: '45 / 51 (88.2 %) are sign-concordant (both CD↑).' The ecotype framework has cross-study variance (LOSO ARI 0.113 from S1) but the operational Tier-A replicates at 88.2% — framework stability and Tier-A replication are distinct properties.

content.title: Six actionable Tier-A pathobionts emerge from 71 scored candidates (threshold score ≥ 2.5)
rows: All 5 A3 signals; 6 BGCs, 4 CD-enriched CB-ORFs
content.caption: Six actionable Tier-A candidates from NB05 scoring of 71 rigor-controlled candidates (51 E1 + 40 E3-provisional + 5 engraftment, dedup). Full scored table in REPORT.md §5g.
content.footnote: Full scored table (71 candidates) in REPORT.md §5g; Tier-B threshold 2.2–2.4.

slides.speaker_notes_seed: The table comes directly from REPORT §5g. Four scoring criteria: A3 literature/cohort CD-association (0–5), A4 protective-analog exclusion (binary), A5 engraftment/strain-adaptation (0/0.5/1), A6 BGC inflammatory mediator (0/0.5/1). Total range 0–4; threshold 2.5 selects 6 of 71. H. hathewayi leads at 4.0 despite being less studied than E. coli — it passes all 5 A3 signals and has 6 BGCs with 4 CD-enriched CB-ORFs. M. gnavus has the largest BGC signal (39 BGCs, 26 CD-enriched). E. coli is AIEC-subset-specific — the strain-resolution requirement matters for phage targeting, which S3 addresses. Note denominator: all 6 ranks are from the 71-candidate pool; Tier-B (score 2.2–2.4) is a separate group not on this slide.

content.title: Targets co-occur in one pathobiont module per ecotype; E3 Tier-A is preliminary evidence pending replication
bullets: E1 co-occurrence network (NB06): 4–5 of 6 Tier-A targets sit in a single module (E1_CD module 0, size 75) — consistent with shared bile-acid dysregulation and low-oxygen inflammation driving co-abundance

E3 Tier-A (40 candidates from HallAB_2017 only, 22 CD / 31 nonIBD) is preliminary evidence for an E3-specific target set; replication is blocked pending HMP2 E3 ingestion (only 10 E3 subjects in HMP2)
Six replicated E1 targets; E3-assigned patients (31% of UC Davis) inherit the provisional E3 list — cocktail recommendations for E3 patients require explicit uncertainty framing in S3

slides.speaker_notes_seed: Two claims on this slide; denominators differ — flag explicitly. First bullet (A7): denominator is the 6 actionable Tier-A targets, of which 4–5 sit in one module per subnet (REPORT §5h). The module structure is consistent with shared ecological conditions (bile-acid dysregulation, low-oxygen inflammation) rather than direct competition — this matters for cocktail design because co-targeting 3+ module members should have compounding effects. Second bullet (A6, partial): denominator is the 40-candidate E3 provisional list, NOT the 51 E1 meta-viable list. HMP2 cannot rescue E3 replication (only 10 E3 subjects). Language discipline: do NOT say 'E3 Tier-A confirms' or 'demonstrates'; say 'preliminary evidence for.' The handoff line: 'Six targets are identified, the E1 set replicates at 88.2% — the next question is whether phage can actually hit them.' That is S3's opening.
